# Chipzen SDK

> Client libraries, wire protocol specs, starters and docs for building bots that compete on Chipzen (chipzen.ai). This index covers Big Bad Bots (game type `bigbadbots`), the robot-fighting game in beta: a bot buys a body, bids in a sealed-bid auction for parts, fits them, then fights one action per tick, ten ticks a second. Bots are written in Python on `chipzen.BigBadBotsBot` (checked locally with `chipzen validate`) or in JavaScript on `BigBadBotsBot` from `@chipzen-ai/bot` (checked with `chipzen-sdk validate`), packaged as a Docker image, and uploaded to chipzen.ai (or staging.chipzen.ai).

Key facts for an agent building a Big Bad Bots bot:

- There is no local simulator. The game engine is private and runs on the platform only. Iterate by uploading the bot and challenging the house bots; `chipzen validate` is the local pre-upload check.
- Subclass `chipzen.BigBadBotsBot` and implement `act()` (one fight tick). `choose_body()`, `bid()` and `fit()` have legal defaults.
- The per-tick response window is 250 ms plus a 3 s time bank per seat for the whole match, never refilled between rounds. `match_start` announces both in `game_config.response_clock` (`deadline_ms`, `time_bank_ms`, `bank_scope`); `state.rules.deadline` still shows the rule set's older numbers (100 ms, a bank per round), so do not read the clock from there.
- Every tick needs its own answer: send `block` again on every tick you want to block.
- While the opponent winds up a move it shows only as `"attack"` in phase `"startup"`.
- Read every number from `state.rules` (the rule set the match is played under); never hard-code one.
- Big Bad Bots support is in `chipzen-bot` 0.5.0 and later on PyPI; the Dockerfile check in `chipzen validate` needs 0.6.0: `pip install "chipzen-bot~=0.6"`.
- JavaScript: Big Bad Bots support is in `@chipzen-ai/bot` 0.4.0 and later on npm; the Dockerfile check in `chipzen-sdk validate` needs 0.5.0: `npm install @chipzen-ai/bot@^0.5.0`. The JavaScript names are the Python ones in camelCase (`chooseBody()`, `state.me.strikeRange`).

## Big Bad Bots docs

- [Big Bad Bots quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/BIGBADBOTS-QUICKSTART.md): from nothing to an uploaded bot fighting the house bots, using a starter as the worked example
- [Big Bad Bots quickstart, JavaScript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/BIGBADBOTS-QUICKSTART-JAVASCRIPT.md): the same walkthrough with `@chipzen-ai/bot` and the JavaScript Rusher starter
- [AGENTS.md build guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/starters/bigbadbots/AGENTS.md): instructions for coding agents: setup, commands, hard rules, done checklist
- [Developer manual, Big Bad Bots chapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/DEV-MANUAL.md): section 10 covers `BigBadBotsBot`, the per-tick budget, blocking every tick, the masked opponent, auction basics, `state.rules`, `chipzen validate` and the on-platform loop
- [Common pitfalls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/COMMON-PITFALLS.md): entries 21 to 29 are the Big Bad Bots mistakes that cost fights
- [Big Bad Bots game state protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/protocol/BIGBADBOTS-GAME-STATE-PROTOCOL.md): the authoritative wire spec: every payload, masking, timing and the semantic rules
- [Rule sets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/docs/RULESETS.md): rule-set ids, lifecycle, the parameter table sections, and the changelog (launch rule set `bigbadbots-1.2`)

## Starters

- [Starters overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/starters/bigbadbots/README.md): the three starters and what each one plays like
- [Rusher bot.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/starters/bigbadbots/rusher/bot.py): aggressive: strikes first, throws blockers, reads frame data from the rule set
- [Zoner bot.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/starters/bigbadbots/zoner/bot.py): spacing: holds the tip of its kick range, steps out of wind-ups
- [Turtle bot.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/starters/bigbadbots/turtle/bot.py): defensive: blocks every tick, punishes whiffs, plays the round clock
- [Rusher bot.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/javascript/starters/bigbadbots/rusher/bot.js): the Rusher starter in JavaScript, answer for answer the same as bot.py

## SDK source

- [chipzen.bigbadbots_bot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/src/chipzen/bigbadbots_bot.py): the `BigBadBotsBot` base class and the protocol default answers
- [chipzen.bigbadbots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/src/chipzen/bigbadbots.py): the state models (`BodyShopState`, `AuctionState`, `FittingState`, `FightState`)
- [chipzen.bigbadbots_rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/python/src/chipzen/bigbadbots_rules.py): `state.rules` and the bundled published rule sets
- [@chipzen-ai/bot bigbadbots_bot.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/javascript/src/bigbadbots_bot.ts): the JavaScript `BigBadBotsBot` and the protocol default answers
- [@chipzen-ai/bot bigbadbots.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chipzen-ai/chipzen-sdk/main/packages/javascript/src/bigbadbots.ts): the JavaScript state models and `RuleSet`
